headline: Franklin Templeton picks Saurabh Arora to head HR in India
summary: Global investment management firm Franklin Templeton has appointed Saurabh Arora as its new Head of HR in India, based in Mumbai. Arora brings extensive financial sector experience to the role, having previously held senior HR leadership positions at Morgan Stanley, Russell Investments, and Waterfield Advisors. In his new capacity, he will focus on talent management, workplace culture, and driving business growth to strengthen the firm's operations in India.

headline: Employee strikes and protests intensify across regions
summary: A rising wave of labor protests and strikes is escalating across India, South Korea, and Spain as workers push for fair pay, job security, and safer working conditions. Beyond traditional workplace issues, these collective actions also address broader socio-economic challenges, including severe housing affordability crises. The widespread disruptions highlight growing international pressure on both employers and governments to resolve long-standing labor and cost-of-living grievances.

headline: Bihar boosts employee earnings and career growth with fresh HR-focused measures
summary: The Bihar Cabinet has approved a 3% increase in dearness allowance and relief for state government employees and retirees to help offset rising living costs. Additionally, the government implemented financial progression schemes for urban local body staff to address career stagnation alongside launching workforce initiatives like the Bihar Artificial Intelligence Mission.

headline: Qualcomm layoffs raise questions over severance support for affected employees in India
summary: Qualcomm has initiated global workforce cuts, including in India, due to slowing demand and rising costs in its core smartphone-chip business. Impacted employees are receiving tenure-based severance packages as the chipmaker shifts focus toward AI infrastructure, data centers, and automotive technologies.

headline: HR Perspectives by Rajendra Mehta: “HR must understand the philosophy behind every practice”
summary: Veteran HR leader Rajendra Mehta emphasizes that HR professionals must understand human behavior and organizational context rather than simply replicating external frameworks. He notes that strategic misalignment and unaddressed leadership dynamics, rather than just compensation, are major drivers behind the exit of capable employees.

headline: Sharmistha Ray joins American India Foundation as director – HR
summary: Sharmistha Ray has been appointed as the Director of Human Resources at the American India Foundation (AIF), bringing over two decades of HR leadership experience across corporate and development sectors. In her new role, Ray will oversee AIF's overarching people strategy, talent management, and HR governance to support the organization's growing scale. She previously led human resources at Tech Mahindra Foundation and held key management roles at Concorde Motors, UST Global, and Agilent Technologies.

headline: Birlasoft elevates Madhavan Hariharan to CEO & MD
summary: Birlasoft has appointed Madhavan Hariharan as its new Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, succeeding Angan Guha. Hariharan, who has served as the group's head of strategy and chief financial officer since 2018, brings over 26 years of executive experience across international organizations. Company Chairman Amita Birla highlighted Hariharan's strategic vision and deep familiarity with the business as key drivers for leading Birlasoft's next phase of growth.

headline: 62% of women in tech say AI eases workloads, yet 42% face higher productivity expectations
summary: According to a survey by Ensono, while 62% of female technology professionals report that AI makes their workloads more manageable, 42% face increased expectations to produce more work in less time. Despite high adoption rates and confidence in their AI skills, 87% of respondents report experiencing burnout, driven primarily by these heightened productivity demands and expectations of constant availability.

headline: MP to build awareness of Labour Codes with Shram Samvad
summary: The Ministry of Labour and Employment, alongside the Madhya Pradesh government, hosted the 'Shram Samvad' awareness programme in Dewas to educate business leaders on India's new Labour Codes. The initiative focused on helping HR, legal, and finance professionals understand compliance responsibilities, operational frameworks, and key social-security schemes. Over 100 industry representatives attended technical sessions and received compliance guides to facilitate smooth implementation.

headline: Suman Saurav takes charge as head-HR at Hindustan Zinc’s Debari operations
summary: Hindustan Zinc has appointed Suman Saurav as the Head of HR for its Zinc Smelter Debari unit and Central Research and Development Laboratory. Saurav, who previously served as the facility's Deputy CHRO, transitions with extensive people management experience alongside a technical operational background from his tenure at Bharat Aluminium Company.

headline: Qantas plans to cut 850 jobs
summary: Qantas plans to eliminate approximately 850 corporate roles over several years as part of a partnership with Accenture to modernize its legacy systems and expand AI adoption. The restructuring will outsource functions in finance, HR, procurement, and marketing, with a significant portion of work transitioning to teams in India. While Qantas leadership intends to consult unions and explore redeployment options before the mid-2027 rollout, the move has sparked criticism regarding overseas job transfers.

headline: Why professionals keep applying for jobs they don’t want
summary: Driven by uncertainty, workplace boredom, and frictionless AI application tools, professionals are increasingly engaging in 'doomjobbing' by compulsively applying for roles they have little intention of accepting. HR experts warn that this trend overwhelms recruiters with irrelevant submissions and distracts workers from building valuable skills that provide genuine job security.

headline: Nvidia faces leadership test as board investigates CEO Jensen Huang
summary: Nvidia's board of directors has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang following disclosures regarding a personal relationship with an executive linked to national security concerns involving chip movements to China. The controversy has raised significant governance and continuity concerns for the AI giant, where the Huang family maintains deep operational and ownership ties. Depending on the inquiry's findings, market analysts note that the board may ultimately be forced to consider leadership changes.

headline: HITL: Why the human is still in the loop
summary: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) AI systems aim to combine automated efficiency with human judgment, context, and oversight. However, in functions like human resources, oversight can easily become a rubber-stamp formality due to automation bias and high workload pressures. To maintain true accountability, organizations must ensure human reviewers possess the time, authority, and information required to meaningfully challenge AI outputs.

headline: UK moves towards mandatory pay transparency in job ads
summary: The UK government is proposing mandatory pay transparency laws that will require employers to include salary details in all job advertisements. Designed to reduce gender pay disparities and assist young jobseekers, the initiative has received strong support from both the public and local businesses. The policy is part of a broader national strategy to enhance youth employment and expand vocational career pathways.

headline: ITC Savlon sings a warning about India’s love of antibiotics
summary: ITC-owned hygiene brand Savlon has launched a new campaign addressing the widespread practice of self-medicating with antibiotics in India. The musical ad highlights the risks of taking unprescribed medication for minor ailments and encourages consumers to consult doctors while practicing handwashing to prevent infections. This initiative continues Savlon's broader strategy of using public health awareness to reinforce hand hygiene and infection control.

headline: David Schwimmer revisits Friends' iconic red sweater moment for Quince
summary: Fashion retailer Quince has launched a holiday campaign starring actor David Schwimmer, who recreates his iconic red sweater storyline from the sitcom Friends to promote the brand's cashmere line. The campaign leverages nostalgia to drive customer engagement, reflecting a broader marketing strategy of using classic television references in major advertisements.

headline: Sony Pictures Networks bags digital, TV rights for Hanuman Ansh
summary: Sony Pictures Networks India has acquired the digital and television broadcasting rights for the spiritual drama film Hanuman Ansh. The movie, inspired by the life of Neem Karoli Baba, is set to premiere on the streaming service Sony LIV on November 27 before airing on Sony MAX. The acquisition expands SPNI's media portfolio by adding family-focused spiritual content to its digital and linear platforms.

headline: Amazon rolls out AI-powered text shopping through Alexa
summary: Amazon has introduced a text-based shopping feature for Alexa in the US, enabling select customers to search, compare products, and complete purchases via text message. The feature will see a broader rollout in the coming weeks following an initial testing phase. The move comes amid ongoing efforts by Amazon to restrict rival third-party AI shopping agents from accessing its e-commerce platform.

headline: How PNG Jewellers is giving Diwali a musical identity with Khushiyon Ki Sargam
summary: PNG Jewellers has launched a digital Diwali campaign titled 'Khushiyon Ki Sargam,' featuring an all-female musical ensemble of six artists. By building the narrative around seven musical notes, the campaign creates a contemporary festive expression that links directly to the brand's Saptam jewellery collection. The initiative aims to differentiate the legacy retailer by making music, rather than traditional visual clichés, the primary storytelling device.

headline: Campa Cola makes festive preparations the star of its new campaign
summary: Campa Cola has launched a new festive campaign titled 'Tayyari Big, Tyohaar Bada Big,' created by McCann India, which focuses on the hectic preparation phase of Indian festivals rather than just the final celebrations. The initiative aims to differentiate the brand in a crowded advertising market by positioning the beverage as a refreshing break during the setup process across television, digital, and social media.

headline: Pernod Ricard names Initiative media agency for India and APAC
summary: Pernod Ricard has named Initiative as its new media agency partner across nine markets in India and the Asia-Pacific region following a competitive review. Replacing long-time incumbent Wavemaker, Initiative will manage media planning, buying, and consumer insights with a focus on brand-building and media innovation. The initial two-year mandate takes effect on January 1, 2027, with an option for a one-year extension.

headline: Marico to acquire 51% stake in Bonorizon for up to Rs 35 crore
summary: Indian FMCG company Marico has agreed to acquire a 51% stake in Bonorizon Consumer Ventures for up to Rs 35 crore in cash to expand its international presence and digital growth. The deal is expected to close within 90 days, with Marico holding an option to acquire the remaining equity after three years based on performance milestones.

headline: Voltas appoints Sunil D’Souza as chairman
summary: Voltas has appointed current board director Sunil D’Souza as its new chairman, effective November 12, 2026. He will succeed Noel N. Tata, who is retiring upon reaching the mandatory superannuation age and will assume the role of chairman emeritus. Additionally, the company announced that Jayant Balan will take over as managing director for a five-year term starting May 25, 2027, following the end of Mukundan Menon C.P.'s tenure.

headline: Airtel appoints Vishwajeet Sinha as vice president- marketing
summary: Telecom giant Airtel has appointed Vishwajeet Sinha as its new Vice President of Marketing. Prior to this role, Sinha served as the marketing and revenue growth lead for Razorpay's SME and cross-border payments division. His professional background also includes senior marketing leadership positions at consumer and tech brands such as Scapia, Meesho, Flipkart, and Larsen & Toubro.

headline: Cathay Cargo’s Dominic Perret on AI cargo boom, Hong Kong’s Edge | Conversations
source_publication: Transportation | Logistics | Aviation | Shipping | Supply Chain
summary: Cathay Cargo reported strong revenue and tonnage growth driven by rising demand for data-centre and AI hardware, expecting this market momentum to persist through 2027. To support its operational vision, the carrier is expanding its Greater Bay Area logistics network and modernizing its fleet with A350Fs and ATSG-leased aircraft. Additionally, Cathay Cargo is integrating specialized AI solutions to streamline compliance, safety screening, and customer service.
